name: Databricks theme palette
note: Single source of truth for every colour used by the two theme files. Only the values under `brand` are official Databricks brand colours; everything under `ramps`, `supporting`, `deep` and `bright` is extrapolated from them so the theme has enough steps to work with. Swap values here (and regenerate/adjust the theme JSON) to re-tune the whole theme in one place.

lava.note: Accent ramp. `lava600` is the brand colour; the other steps are derived. Numbering skips 500 so `lava600` keeps the official 'Lava 600' name.

navy.note: Neutral spine. `navy800` and `navy900` are brand colours; the lighter steps and `navy850` (the dark-variant surface, sitting between the two brand navies) are derived.

oat.note: Light neutrals. `oatWhite`, `oatLight` and `oatMedium` are brand colours; `oatDark` and `oatDeep` are derived.

supporting.note: Syntax and status hues. Seven hues spread evenly around the wheel (approximate hue angles: amber 37, green 92, teal 168, cyan 192, blue 223, purple 265, magenta 318) so adjacent tokens never land in the same wedge. Lava sits at hue 7 at full chroma and is deliberately the only colour in the warm-red wedge — no supporting hue is allowed to compete with it there. The same role keeps the same hue family in both variants; only lightness shifts.

deep.note: Darker steps used in the light variant wherever a hue sits on the Oat Medium secondary surface (side bar, panel) instead of the Oat Light editor background — the base hues clear 4.5:1 on the editor background but some do not on the surface. In the dark variant the base hues already clear it, so `deep` mirrors `supporting.dark`.

bright.note: Terminal 'bright' ANSI steps. Light-mode brights go deeper (a lighter bright-green is unreadable on an Oat background), so they reuse the `deep` ramp; dark-mode brights go lighter.

roles.note: How the ramps map onto each variant. The theme JSON files are the authority; this block documents the intent.

syntax.note: Which hue carries which syntactic role, in both variants.

alpha.note: Alpha suffixes used for translucent layers, so selection, find match, word highlight and the tinted UI surfaces stack legibly.
